name: vwap_mean_reversion_5s_3
author: adapted from AI_Quant
thesis: This strategy exploits intraday mean reversion to VWAP. In range-bound or oscillating markets, price often spikes away and then returns to the VWAP (seen as the intraday 'fair value' line)【8†L137-L142】. This inefficiency arises from short-term overreactions and institutional VWAP-centric execution. It persists because many traders under-utilize VWAP and because reverting trades require precise timing amid noise.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

conditions: close < vwap AND vwap_zscore < -1.5 AND volume > 2 * avgvol30
close > vwap AND vwap_zscore > 1.5 AND volume > 2 * avgvol30

weaknesses: Fails in strong trending regimes (trend continues beyond VWAP)
Relies on accurate VWAP calculation, can give false signals in low volume
Potential slippage if reversal is sharp (fast moves)
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
